articles.title: Campari is making its biggest bet ever on a pink spritz
articles.summary: As the alcohol industry deals with a dreary environment in the US, Aperol’s parent company hopes a brightly colored aperitif imported from Italy will entice drinkers.
articles.body: As the alcohol industry deals with a dreary environment in the US, Aperol’s parent company hopes a brightly colored aperitif imported from Italy will entice drinkers. Campari Group is making its biggest investment ever for the US launch of Sarti Rosa, a tropical pink-colored aperitivo liqueur made for spritzes. The Sarti Spritz has built a devoted following from Americans visiting Europe over the past few years, posting the bubbly concoction on TikTok and begging the company to bring it stateside. The Italian company has seen its US business grow consecutively for the past five years by heavily promoting Aperol and Campari, popularizing the spritz to Americans cutting back on drinking as a lighter alternative to booze-heavy cocktails. With Sarti Rosa, however, the aim is to attract younger drinkers who prefer a sweeter aperitivo that doesn’t taste bitter. “There’s a lot more growth in the spritz category,” Allison Varone, head of marketing for Campari Group, told CNN. “We believe that (Sarti Rosa) is building upon that and consumers now know what a spritz is, so they’re looking for different spins and variations.” For those unfamiliar, a Sarti Spritz has tasting notes of mango, passionfruit and blood orange that is mixed with Prosecco and club soda. The pink-hued cocktail is photogenic, which has made it a social media sensation. For the first six months of this year, global sales of Campari Group’s aperitifs, including Aperol and Campari, grew 4%. The category that includes Sarti Rosa jumped nearly 9% worldwide, bolstered by the pink drink’s continued growth across Europe. Sales for many alcohol brands in the US market have been sluggish as consumers in recent years, particularly younger ones, moderate their drinking or seek out more budget-friendly options. “The alcohol business in the United States is struggling more than in virtually any other part of the world,” Bourcard Nesin, a beverage analyst for Rabobank, told CNN earlier this year. “We’re seeing dramatic declines in consumption that aren’t taking place elsewhere.” However, early signs in the United States have been encouraging for Campari Group. The company began rolling out Sarti Rosa to retailers and bars in June. Southern Glazer’s Wine and Spirits, the nation’s biggest distributor, told CNN that the liqueur is one of its most successful launches ever. “We are seeing particular success in markets that already over-index with spritz, like New York,” said Zach Poelma, the company’s senior vice president of strategy and insights. “While normally a new item launch would build up over time and be a more gradual build, we are seeing significant interest from both chains and independent accounts.” At Saksey’s, a cocktail bar in Detroit, the Sarti Spritz has become one of the bar’s top-selling drinks since hitting menus last month. Tara Wong, head bartender, attributes its quick rise to a growing thirst among drinkers for refreshing, fruit-forward options. “What has been especially exciting is that guests are not only asking for the Sarti Spritz, they are interested in experiencing it in other cocktails as well,” Wong told CNN. Sarti’s debut comes amid growing competition for spritzes in the United States, including from the Hugo Spritz, an elderflower-based cocktail often made from Bacardi-owned St-Germain. The privately held company hasn’t disclosed St-Germain sales. But in June, a research note from S&P Global said the liqueur continues “to grow faster than the broader industry.” Square data shows that orders have skyrocketed more than 150% year-over-year, making the Hugo Spritz the fastest-growing cocktail this past summer. Despite the competition, Campari Group’s Varone said she thinks the US launch of Sarti Rosa will help bolster Campari’s dominance within spritz. “We’re fortunate that we lean in on a portfolio that’s attractive to all consumers, especially young ones,” she said.

articles.title: Big dollar inflows, little boost for rupee: Why the currency may stay near Rs 96 in near term
articles.summary: After suffering multiple lows over the year, rupee may now see some stability against the US dollar.
articles.body: After suffering multiple lows over the year, rupee may now see some stability against the US dollar. The currency is likely to remain in the Rs 94.5-96 per dollar range in the near term, despite sizeable dollar inflows through FCNR deposits and external commercial borrowings (ECBs), according to a Bank of Baroda research report.The report said the inflows have largely gone into the Reserve Bank of India's reserves instead of entering the market. This has limited the extent to which the additional dollar supply could have translated into appreciation in rupee.“In the current situation a range of Rs 94.5-96 looks likely in the near term,” the report said. It added that sharp appreciation of the rupee, which could theoretically have followed the increase in dollar inflows, has been limited as the inflows “have not been infused into the market but added to reserves.”The report's analysis suggests that the exchange rate cannot be explained by dollar flows or any other individual factor in isolation. Rupee movements have been shaped by a combination of fundamentals, intervention by the RBI and market sentiment.The domestic currency has lost around 28 per cent since January 2022. The rupee's average exchange rate moved from Rs 74.44 per dollar in January 2022 to Rs 95.47 in August 2026.Other Asian currencies also weakened during this period, although to varying degrees. The yen depreciated by 38 per cent, while the Indonesian rupiah and South Korean won fell 24 per cent and 17 per cent, respectively. In comparison, the dollar gained 2.4 per cent against the euro.To assess what has been driving these movements, the Bank of Baroda report examined monthly currency data between January 2022 and June 2026. Its analysis covered changes in foreign exchange reserves, RBI operations in spot and forward markets, FPI flows and movements in the dollar-euro exchange rate.RBI intervention emerged as one of the variables with a significant relationship with rupee movements. The relationship was stronger when spot and forward interventions were considered together. Their combined explanatory power stood at 34 per cent, against 25 per cent for spot intervention alone and 19 per cent for forward operations alone.The report said this finding suggests that the RBI's use of both spot and forward operations together could be more effective in managing the currency.Forex reserves, on the other hand, had a relatively limited explanatory power of 18 per cent. The report said this indicates that even a sharp rise in reserves following dollar inflows does not necessarily produce a major movement in the exchange rate.FPI flows also showed a significant relationship with the rupee when examined separately. However, that significance disappeared once the other variables were considered alongside FPI flows.“The factors driving the exchange rate are through multiple routes and separating them statistically does not reveal any dominant variable,” the report said.The analysis found that the variables studied explained no more than 40 per cent of the variation in the rupee. A substantial portion of the movement remained outside what the analysis could capture.The report attributed much of this unexplained component to sentiment, including the timing of dollar purchases by importers and exporters and the flow of remittances.The findings therefore point to a currency market where movements are influenced through several channels rather than being driven by one dominant variable. articles.title: Why FIIs may not return to Indian stocks even after AI boom fades
articles.summary: Foreign investors may continue to remain cautious on Indian stocks even after the artificial intelligence (AI) trade peaks, brokerage Bernstein said.
articles.body: Foreign investors may continue to remain cautious on Indian stocks even after the artificial intelligence (AI) trade peaks, brokerage Bernstein said. It said foreign investors are unlikely to return in large numbers unless India is able to build industries and companies that can compete globally, making this a key factor for a sustained recovery in foreign investment.Bernstein expects foreign institutional investor (FII) flows to stay flat to slightly positive over the next 12 months. However, it said this would mainly show that some of the recent pressures on foreign investors have eased, rather than a major improvement in the factors that drive their long-term investment decisions.“We do not believe FIIs will return in large numbers even after the AI trade peaks,” the brokerage said.For foreign investors to return in a sustained way, India will need to create “new engines of competitiveness, innovation, and global relevance”, Bernstein said.The brokerage said India needs to show stronger capabilities in areas such as advanced semiconductor manufacturing, batteries and energy storage, and energy self-sufficiency.It also needs businesses that can win a meaningful share of global markets, Bernstein said.There are some early signs of this in sectors such as space, defence, semiconductors and deep-tech. However, most of these sectors are still too small to have a major impact on global investment decisions, it said.The comments come after a sharp change in foreign investment flows into Indian equities. FIIs have pulled out USD 40 billion from Indian stocks over the last two years.Over the past 24 months, FIIs recorded combined outflows of USD 56.3 billion. This compares with inflows of USD 38.6 billion in the 24 months before that.Bernstein said the link between India’s economic growth and FII flows has weakened. The earlier link between the interest-rate difference between India and the US and FII flows has also faded.Foreign investors are now paying more attention to currency movements, relative valuations and changes in expected earnings, the brokerage said.The rupee has become an important factor in FII flows. Bernstein said the correlation between FII flows and the currency has risen above 70% in recent years.This may mean that a weaker rupee is reducing the returns foreign investors get when their investments are measured in US dollar terms, it said.High valuations have emerged as another factor.Bernstein said its analysis showed that rising relative valuations have gone along with weaker FII flows in recent years, making it harder to attract foreign capital.The brokerage expects FII flows to remain flat to modestly positive over the next 12 months. But it said this would mainly reflect an easing of recent headwinds and not a major improvement in the factors that drive long-term foreign investment.For a sustained return of foreign capital, Bernstein said India will need to create a new generation of globally competitive companies and build new sources of competitiveness, innovation and global relevance.You use AI every day. articles.title: GIFT Nifty breaks the $23 billion mark as trading activity hits a fresh high
articles.summary: GIFT Nifty's expansion since its full-scale launch in July 2023 has taken the international platform to another trading milestone, with turnover, volume
articles.body: GIFT Nifty's expansion since its full-scale launch in July 2023 has taken the international platform to another trading milestone, with turnover, volume and open interest all hitting fresh highs on September 25.The platform's cumulative turnover reached $3.52 trillion as of September 25, 2026, while more than 76.19 million contracts had been traded since the start of full-scale operations, NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) said in a press release.The latest session added another record to that growth. GIFT Nifty's turnover for the day stood at $23.67 billion, its highest-ever single-day figure, with 5,12,023 contracts changing hands.The platform also ended the session with its highest-ever open interest at $21.87 billion, equivalent to around Rs 2.10 lakh crore. The corresponding number of contracts stood at 4,71,287.Both figures moved past their previous records. The earlier single-day turnover high was $23.48 billion on February 20, 2026, while the previous open interest record of $21.56 billion was set on June 25, 2026.NSE IX described the latest milestones as a “new era for Gift Nifty”. It said trading turnover has been “growing exponentially” since the platform began full-scale operations on July 3, 2023.GIFT Nifty's record session came just a day after another major development involving the National Stock Exchange of India. NSE was listed on the BSE on September 24, with its shares making their debut at Rs 1,800 against an issue price of Rs 1,785. The listing price represented a 0.84 per cent premium.NSE is one of India's leading stock exchanges and provides trading across multiple asset classes. Its unique investor base crossed 11 crore in January 2025. The exchange also processed more than 2,000 crore orders in a single day on July 23, 2024, and around 29 crore trades on June 5, 2024. Both were described as the highest in the world.The international platform behind GIFT Nifty is NSE IX, which was established at GIFT City in 2017 as a multi-asset international exchange. Its offerings cover Indian single-stock and index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks.NSE IX also operates primary-market products covering equity shares, REITs, InvITs and debt securities.The exchange said GIFT Nifty and NSE IX have received regulatory exemptions that allow US customers to participate in derivative contracts listed on NSE IX.
